label: Are you authorized to work in the country you reside or where you are living?*
note: location_country's \bcountry\b pattern matched this before the 'authoriz/eligib/legally/sponsor' negative guard was added. 2,373 corpus fields affected.

label: Will you now or in the future require sponsorship for employment visa status in the country for which this role is based?*
note: location_country's \bcountry\b pattern matched this (round 2, different phrasing) before the 'sponsor' negative guard was added. 864 corpus fields affected.

label: Are you a current or former civilian or military employee of the United States Government? (If yes, when/where were you last employed and what was you
note: Originally added to assert previously_employed_here — real current behavior (post P1.5's 'ever'-pattern addition, verified against this exact corpus label) correctly routes it to the near-duplicate previously_employed capability instead (category_mapping.py documents these as legitimately near-duplicate ontology categories, not a bug). Regression coverage here is really about the location_state/eeo_veteran negative guards this label originally motivated: without them, 'military'/'civilian' would wrongly match location_state or eeo_veteran instead of any previously_employed* capability. If this label ever stops resolving to a previously_employed* capability at all, that's the real regression to catch.

label: Will you now or in the future require sponsorship for employment visa status (e.g., H-1B visa status)?*
note: Matched visa_status's 'visa status' pattern before the 'now or in the future/will you require/require sponsor' negative guard was added. 2,209 corpus fields affected.

label: Do you consider yourself to have a disability, impairment or long-term health condition
note: Matched work_authorized_longterm's long.?term pattern (via 'long-term health condition') before the 'disab/impairment/health condition' negative guard was added. 248 corpus fields affected. Found after P1.5's tier 1-2 spec-compliance rewrite routed more fields through the label tier.

label: Are you currently, or have you ever in the past, been employed by Studs?*
note: previously_employed's original patterns never covered 'have you ever... been employed by <Company>' phrasing. Added ever.*(been employed|worked) pattern. 3,021 corpus fields affected.

label: What is your preferred name/nickname? Please feel free to include phonetic pronunciation
note: phone's unbounded /phone/i pattern matched the substring in 'phonetic', and phone is checked before preferred_name (first-match-wins), so this field was wrongly filled with the user's phone number. Found on the FIRST live browser test, not the corpus. Fixed with a word boundary: \bphone\b.

label: Are you willing to undergo a background check, in accordance with local law/regulations?*
note: New capability (was UNSUPPORTED) — added as part of the consent-policy layer (extension/consent_policy.js). Answered by the policy dispatcher, not resolveValue(). Confirms this label is correctly SEMANTICALLY classified consent_background_check; does not assert anything about the accept/decline answer, which replay never sees.

label: Applicant Privacy Acknowledgement *
note: New capability (was UNSUPPORTED). Regression coverage matters here specifically because 'email' had to gain a gdpr/controller-of-personal-data negative guard to stop stealing consent_gdpr_notice fields, and email/phone gained sms/whatsapp/newsletter/job-openings guards to stop stealing these — this entry (and the two below) guard against those guards ever being silently removed.

label: AtriCure retains personal data for as long as necessary to evaluate applications and manage recruitment activities, in accordance with applicable data protection laws. By selecting “Consent” below, you confirm that you have been informed of your rights under GDPR and that you consent to the processing of your data for talent acquisition purposes.
note: New capability (was UNSUPPORTED). Was misclassified 'email' before email's gdpr/controller-of-personal-data negative guards were added (this exact label's real, unabridged corpus text mentions data-controller/GDPR legal language that has no 'email' substring itself, but the CLASS of long GDPR-notice text this represents did collide with email in other real corpus instances).

label: Do you allow us to provide you TEXT/SMS updates of your interview process? We may engage with a service provider to do so.*
note: New capability (was UNSUPPORTED). Real corpus phrasing like 'contact you via SMS, WhatsApp, phone, or email' was being stolen by email/phone/location_address's bare patterns (560+178+131 fields respectively) before sms/whatsapp negative guards were added to all three.

label: Email me about other job openings within the Booking Holding’s entities and recruitment-related newsletters*
note: New capability (was UNSUPPORTED). This exact label starts with the word 'Email', which was being caught by email's bare pattern (300 fields) before the newsletter/recruitment-notif/job-openings negative guards were added.

label: Myriad360 values diversity in all its forms. To ensure that we comply with reporting requirements and to learn more about how we can increase diversity in our candidate pool, we invite you to voluntarily provide demographic information in a confidential survey at the end of this application. If you choose to fill it out, the responses will be used in aggregate to help us identify areas for improvement in our process. Your responses or whether you complete this survey will not be associated with your specific application and cannot in any way be used in the hiring decision. Would you like to participate?
note: New capability (was CLASSIFICATION_NO_MATCH). Found on the second live browser test of the same job — this exact wording was known from corpus analysis as a one-off (1 company) during the original consent-policy build and deliberately deferred then; added after being confirmed live rather than staying theoretical. Pattern written against the semantic class ('voluntary'/'confidential' + 'demographic'/'diversity' + 'survey'), not this literal sentence, with a negative guard against eeo_gender/eeo_race/eeo_hispanic/eeo_veteran/eeo_disability's keywords so it can never shadow those per-attribute question fields.
